video.title: You’re Being Sold Without Knowing It (How To Copy This Trick)

summary: Neville explains how clear, personal sales writing helped AppSumo sell more deals and changed how he marketed products through House of Rave. He teaches the Attention, Interest, Desire, Action framework and shows how product stories, unexpected use cases, and email format can make an offer more compelling. He also discusses cold email, customer feedback, storytelling, and using ChatGPT Projects with real company materials. His main point is that useful, human-sounding copy and a strong understanding of customers matter more than fancy language or a fixed page length.

tactics.name: Write sales copy in a natural speaking voice
steps: Capture how the founder naturally explains the offer in conversation.
Write down the founder's words as close to verbatim as possible.
Use that personal note as the lead copy on the sales page or in an ad.

tactics.name: Structure a pitch with Attention, Interest, Desire, Action
steps: Get attention with a clear hook.
Build interest with facts, use cases, and testimonials.
Show how the customer's life or work improves if they buy.
Tell them what to do next.

quote.text: Attention, interest, desire, action. That's what every single AppSumo email was based on.

tactics.name: Turn overlooked product uses into sales bullets
steps: Ask buyers how they actually use the product.
Find customer groups beyond the obvious target audience.
Turn those uses into concrete examples and bullet points in the sales pitch.

quote.text: That's a freaking bullet point to put in a sales pitch somewhere that plumbing companies use these.
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Send one short, one medium, then one long cold email
steps: Start with a very short message that sounds like a person wrote it.
Follow with a medium version that adds the main proof and offer.
Send a longer version last to cover the remaining reasons to respond.
Keep UK outreach within the applicable marketing rules, including consent requirements for individuals and sole traders.

quote.text: I say sending out one short one, one medium one, one long one to everyone.
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Balance useful content with sales emails
steps: Include something useful, entertaining, or educational in regular sales emails.
Use Neville's suggested 70% content and 30% sales split as a starting point.
Choose a frequency the team can sustain with useful material.

quote.text: If you are willing to do 70% content and 30% sales, you could email them unlimited and they never get mad.
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Test simple email formats
steps: Test a plain text email with a short subject line and a simple link.
Try a second format with a headline, a product picture, and another short section repeated down the email.
Compare clicks and sales against the current format.

quote.text: And then I'm basically just going to copy this over and over and over.
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Use customer feedback to detect quality problems
steps: Do not treat silence as proof that customers like the product or content.
Look for specific feedback that identifies a fixable issue.
Use recurring customer replies and engagement as signals about long-term quality.

quote.text: For writing really really good copy what you notice is like over the long run people will still reply to newsletters still read it still be influenced by it
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Preserve distinctive human details in creative work
steps: Keep the informal phrasing, rough drawings, or visual quirks that customers respond to.
Use AI to assist with production, but check that the result still sounds and looks like the business.
Compare the polished version with the more personal version.

quote.text: going back to like goofy to where it's just like this is so stupid AI wouldn't have made it
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Give ChatGPT a reusable project brief
steps: Create a ChatGPT Project for the business.
Upload the website, blog, images, PDF decks, and real case studies.
Tell it to reuse the company's stories, numbers, and results when drafting emails.
Review the facts and copy before sending.

quote.text: Upload all your images, all your PDF decks, all that kind of stuff.
quote.speaker: Neville

tactics.name: Keep running a proven ad while its economics work
steps: Track the cost to run the ad and the return it produces.
Continue the ad while the return remains above the cost.
Stop or revise it when the economics no longer make sense.

quote.text: You spend $1,000, you make a,000 plus one, you keep you keep doing it until it makes under that.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a product story rather than an arbitrary word count
steps: Start with a specific, emotionally credible story connected to the product or customer.
Make the copy as long as the story needs, but remove unnecessary repetition.
Judge the result by reader response rather than length alone.

quote.text: I think you wrote a really heartfelt story, right?
quote.speaker: Neville

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest describes first-hand work on House of Rave and AppSumo emails and gives specific methods, but many results are anecdotes without test details. The transcript has noticeable auto-caption errors, and some examples are second-hand historical stories.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Neville promotes his Copywriting Course and community. The host also promotes TK Owners, and the video includes a Beehiiv sponsor read; those ads are not treated as business ideas.
